clue.text: See 20
Bone in front or behind? Hesitant pronouncement

parts.note: the stern is the back end of a ship, so it can stand for behind
um is the sound a speaker makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone unsure whether a certain bone sits at the front or the back of the body, voicing their doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bone in front or behind?' reads as one anatomical question, but the definition stops at 'front'; 'behind' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone sits at the front of the chest, so it is literally a bone in front.

clue.text: In operation nine to five, say

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the word operation

explanation.surface: A business or shop running office hours, nine to five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nine to five' suggests working hours, but here it is written 9:5, a comparison of two numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine to five, written 9:5, is an example of a proportion between two quantities.

clue.text: Gather together in a cold island

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: People huddling for warmth on a chilly island.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to grow by accumulating, so it is a formal synonym for collecting together.

clue.text: Orville or Wilbur, say, making fine catch

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: Orville and Wilbur Wright were the aviation pioneers, so either could be addressed by title and surname

explanation.surface: A Wright brother making a good catch, perhaps in a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The title-plus-surname spoken aloud matches the phrase for an ideal partner, with WRIGHT entered as its sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine catch is a desirable partner, and the idiom for the perfect man fits that exactly.

clue.text: Striker popular with party? True

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a side is one party in a dispute or game
true can mean correct or accurate

explanation.surface: A footballer who is liked by the team and loyal to it.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an old football position, the forward playing just inside the outside man on the attacking flank.
explanation.definitionFit: The named position is a forward in old football formations, and forwards are strikers.

clue.text: Overwhelm with emotion that can move people

explanation.surface: Something powerful enough to carry people away, emotionally or physically.
explanation.definitionFit: To be carried away by feeling is one sense; a means of conveyance for passengers is the other.

clue.text: Ex-president upset — time to withdraw

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Jimmy Carter is a former US president

explanation.surface: A former president, upset, deciding it is time to pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'upset' means turned upside down, so the former president is read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement or pull a claw in is to withdraw it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: School covering 9, 23 and 20

definitions.meaning: a non-selective state secondary school in Britain
taking in all three political positions named by those numbers, so including everything

explanation.surface: A school whose curriculum spans the whole political spectrum.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain this is the standard state secondary school that takes all abilities.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means all-inclusive as well as naming a British type of non-selective secondary school.

clue.text: Omitted to make Conservatives triumphant?

definitions.meaning: not done or not attended to
read whimsically, the political opposition of the Conservatives has been defeated or ruined

explanation.surface: Something neglected which happens to delight the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks not done are neglected; read another way, the opposition party wing is ruined.

clue.text: Rolls in collection of cars isn't so different

indicators.note: different says the letters of the phrase are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Rolls-Royces in a car collection being not so unlike the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' points to the car marque in the surface, but it means bread rolls; 'different' rearranges CARS ISN'T SO.
explanation.definitionFit: These are crescent-shaped French bread rolls, so the plural is an example of rolls.

clue.text: See 9
Base 18 rebuilt over time

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new arrangement

parts.note: the answer to 18 down, a word meaning passed

explanation.surface: A base reconstructed after a period of time has passed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' rearranges ELAPSED with T for time; 'over' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth on which a statue stands is its base, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Authorised printing unit we are getting in school

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of width

indicators.note: getting in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a school of whales or dolphins is also called a pod
we're is the contraction of we are

explanation.surface: Someone authorised to run a printing unit at their school.
explanation.walkthrough: A pod is a school of whales, not a teaching school.
explanation.definitionFit: To be given power to act is to be authorised, a near synonym.

clue.text: Top gear

parts.note: read as clothing put on top of everything else, not a car's highest gear or the TV show

explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a British TV motoring programme, which is the misleading reading; here gear means clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coats and jackets worn over other clothes are gear for the top layer.

clue.text: Of a type of chocolate

parts.note: the two-letter word is what sits in the middle of a four-letter word for squashy, read as an instruction

explanation.surface: A description of a chocolate's variety.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction, take the middle of a word meaning yielding, gives OF.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate with a fondant or cream filling is a familiar type of boxed chocolate.

clue.text: See 23
Remainder zero — all right?

definitions.meaning: whimsically, if the political wing opposite has gone, the whole is the other side

explanation.surface: A sum with no remainder, checked for correctness.
explanation.definitionFit: When none remains the remainder is zero; and with one wing gone all is its opposite.

clue.text: Detect intern — one might be in this

definitions.text: Detect intern — one might be in this

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Spotting an internee, who could well be held in this sort of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' rearranges DETECT INTERN ONE; the whole clue also describes the place, where a detected internee would be held.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is held in a facility for detaining people, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Passed by breaking a speed limit, initially

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters are smashed and rearranged
initially takes only the opening letter of limit

explanation.surface: A driver who went by while breaking the speed limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges A SPEED with L, the first letter of 'limit' as 'initially' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has gone by has passed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Actor I spotted in old musical

indicators.note: spotted in means seen inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's 1960 musical

explanation.surface: Someone spotting themselves in a classic musical.
explanation.walkthrough: OLIVER! is a 1960 British musical based on Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and screen actor.

clue.text: Couple of pages in paper for corporation?

definitions.meaning: the double-page feature across the middle of a newspaper or magazine
a corporation is old British slang for a paunch

explanation.surface: A double page bought by a company for its advertising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is dated British slang for a big belly, a middle-age spread.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle pages of a paper form a double-page layout; a paunch spreads at the waist.

clue.text: Courses for runners, initially

definitions.meaning: the first dishes of a meal
those competing as a race begins

explanation.surface: Racecourses made for runners at the beginning of their careers.
explanation.definitionFit: Opening dishes of a meal are courses; competitors at the start of a race are runners.

clue.text: Perfectly OK ceremony, as a rule, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words are judged by sound, not spelling

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony and a reign is a rule, with as in between

explanation.surface: A ceremony that is usually fine.
explanation.walkthrough: RITE sounds like the first word, REIGN like the last; 'as a rule' looks like the phrase meaning usually.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in perfectly good health or order, so it means perfectly OK.

clue.text: Having entitlement to money, one appropriately struck

parts.note: an entitlement is a claim one is due
a banknote is money

explanation.surface: Someone entitled to cash who has been fairly hit.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is to strike the suitable tone, so a musical sound appropriately struck.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying exactly the fitting thing is striking a suitable tone, the phrase for a well-judged sound.

clue.text: Instructions from dreadful court composer

parts.note: dire means dreadful
Charles Ives was an American composer

explanation.surface: Orders issued by a terrible royal court composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Directives are official orders, so they are instructions.

clue.text: Forbidding German to go west of border

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so this piece comes first

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A stern German heading west of the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbidding expression is stern and harsh, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A growing concern

parts.note: read as a business that is concerned with growing plants, not one that is expanding

explanation.walkthrough: A going concern is a thriving business; here 'growing' is literal horticulture.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling plants and gardening supplies is a business concerned with things that grow.

clue.text: One prepares to publish something, having partly revised it, originally

indicators.note: partly says only part of the phrase is used, the letters running across the words

explanation.surface: Someone getting a work ready for publication after revising some of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' points to letters inside REVISED IT ORIGINALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: This person prepares text for publication, which is exactly what the definition describes.
